title: fix(agents): run async native tools on the kickoff caller's event loop
body:
Fixes #8904.

Follow-up to #7630 (the closed #7634 was the pre-#8192 fix for the same family).

## The bug (reproduced on `main`)

After #8192, every sync Flow method runs in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`, flow runtime `_execute_method`). An async native tool's coroutine therefore goes through the bare `asyncio.run()` inside `Tool.run` — on a **fresh, unrelated event loop per call**. Anything bound to the kickoff caller's loop fails deterministically:

```
RuntimeError: Task ... got Future <Future pending> attached to a different loop
```

Minimal repro on unpatched `main`: a Crew with one `@tool async def`; the tool awaits a `Future` created on the `kickoff_async` caller's loop after `asyncio.run(crew.kickoff_async())` → the tool result the LLM sees is `Error executing tool: ... attached to a different loop`. Same shape for any caller-loop-bound resource (`httpx.AsyncClient` created before kickoff, sockets).

## The fix

- The async kickoffs capture the caller's event loop into a **ContextVar** (`Crew.kickoff_async` non-stream branch, `AgentExecutor.invoke_async`). `Crew.kickoff_async` is `await asyncio.to_thread(self.kickoff, ...)`, so capturing **before** the thread boundary is what makes the loop visible inside every worker lane — ContextVars propagate through `to_thread` and the Flow runtime's `copy_context` (including the `ThreadPoolExecutor` in `execute_native_tool`).
- `agent_utils.run_native_tool_result(...)` executes the tool: when a caller loop is present **and** the tool has a working async implementation, bridge `tool.arun(**args)` onto the caller loop via `run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` (the worker thread blocks; the coroutine runs with caller-loop affinity). Otherwise the exact historical sync behavior — the `available_functions` mapping stays authoritative, so test doubles and cache wrappers are untouched.
- Async-capability detection: `Tool`-wrapped functions are async iff the wrapped function is a coroutine function (`Tool` always overrides `_arun`, even for sync funcs); class-based `BaseTool`s qualify when their type overrides the `NotImplementedError`-raising `BaseTool._arun`.

## Tests

New `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_native_async_tool_loop_affinity.py`:

- worker-thread bridge onto a caller-loop `Future` (unit, with and without caller loop),
- full `Crew` + scripted-LLM `kickoff_async` path asserting the caller-loop Future **resolves** instead of the cross-loop error.

## Verification

- `ruff check` clean on all touched files.
- A/B vs pristine `main`: `pytest lib/crewai/tests/agents -k "native or agent_executor or invoke"` — **identical failure sets** (3 pre-existing `TestDeferredNativeToolResults` / `TestResponseFormatWithKickoff` failures reproduce on pristine `main` in this environment; 172 pass on both), plus 4 new green tests.
- With the patch, the repro above returns `got:expected-item` instead of the error.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core async kickoff and native-tool concurrency (ContextVar bridging, thread pools, blocking waits); behavior is scoped and heavily tested but affects all async kickoff + async tool combinations.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes async native tools breaking under **`kickoff_async`** when sync Flow work runs in worker threads: coroutines no longer spin up a fresh loop per call, so caller-loop-bound resources (e.g. **`httpx.AsyncClient`**, **`Future`s**) stop failing with *attached to a different loop*.
> 
> **Caller-loop capture:** **`Crew.kickoff_async`** (streaming and non-streaming) and **`AgentExecutor.invoke_async`** store the running loop in a **ContextVar** for the duration of the run, so worker-thread tool paths can see it after **`to_thread`** / context copy.
> 
> **Tool execution:** Native tool dispatch in **`agent_executor`** and **`agent_utils`** now goes through **`run_native_tool_result`**, which schedules **`tool.arun`** on that loop via **`run_coroutine_threadsafe`** when the tool is async; sync tools and missing-loop cases keep the old **`run()`** behavior. Bridging skips when already on the target loop (deadlock guard), propagates tool errors without double execution, and times out after **`CREWAI_NATIVE_TOOL_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT`** (default 300s) with coroutine cancellation.
> 
> **Executor pool split:** Sync **`kickoff`** bodies move from the loop’s default **`asyncio.to_thread`** pool to a dedicated **`run_in_kickoff_thread`** pool so kickoff threads waiting on bridged tools don’t starve the default pool when tools use **`asyncio.to_thread`** inside their coroutines.
> 
> Regression coverage is added in **`test_native_async_tool_loop_affinity.py`** (bridge behavior, E2E **`kickoff_async`**, streaming path, concurrent kickoffs, inherited **`_arun`**).

title: [BUG] Async native tools run on a per-call event loop, so caller-loop-bound resources fail under kickoff_async
body:
### Description

Async native tools lose the kickoff caller's event loop. When a crew is started with `kickoff_async()` (or `AgentExecutor.invoke_async()`), the sync lane runs in worker threads, and the native tool call path awaits the tool's coroutine via a bare `asyncio.run()` on a **fresh, unrelated event loop per call**.

Any resource bound to the caller's loop — a caller-loop `asyncio.Future`, an `httpx.AsyncClient` created before kickoff, a websocket/socket — therefore fails deterministically:

```
Error executing tool: The future belongs to a different loop than the one specified as the loop argument
```

(same family as #7630, still present on `main` after #8192 promoted `AgentExecutor` out of experimental; the loop-affinity surface just moved from "`asyncio.run` inside the running loop" to "`asyncio.run` in a worker thread").

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import asyncio, json
from typing import Any

from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.llms.base_llm import BaseLLM
from crewai.tools import tool

HOLDER: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}


@tool("async_probe")
async def async_probe(query: str) -> str:
    """Await a caller-loop-bound future, then report what it returned."""
    fut = HOLDER.pop("fut", None)
    if fut is None:
        return f"async-ok:{query}"
    return f"got:{await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout=2)}"


class ScriptedLLM(BaseLLM):
    """Stub LLM: emit one native tool call, then a final answer."""

    def __init__(self, responses: list[Any]) -> None:
        super().__init__(model="stub-model")
        self._responses = list(responses)
        self.calls: list[list[dict[str, Any]]] = []

    def supports_function_calling(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def supports_stop_words(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def call(self, messages, tools=None, available_functions=None, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append(list(messages))
        step = self._responses.pop(0)
        if isinstance(step, tuple) and step[0] == "tool":
            return step[1]
        return str(step)


tool_call = [{
    "id": "call_1",
    "type": "function",
    "function": {"name": "async_probe", "arguments": json.dumps({"query": "hello"})},
}]
llm = ScriptedLLM([("tool", tool_call), "final answer"])
agent = Agent(
    role="worker", goal="use the tools", backstory="agent", llm=llm,
    tools=[async_probe], allow_delegation=False, max_iter=6,
)
task = Task(description="use the tool", expected_output="the result", agent=agent)
crew = Crew(agents=[agent], tasks=[task], process=Process.sequential)


async def scenario() -> None:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    fut = loop.create_future()
    loop.call_later(0.05, fut.set_result, "expected-item")
    HOLDER["fut"] = fut
    await crew.kickoff_async()


asyncio.run(scenario())
```

1. Save the snippet as `repro.py` and run it on current `main` (`f04cce923`).
2. The async tool's coroutine runs on a per-call loop, so awaiting the caller-loop future raises.
3. The LLM sees the failure as the tool result.

### Expected behavior

An async native tool executed during an async kickoff should run with the kickoff caller's loop affinity, so loop-bound resources created before kickoff keep working. The tool result the LLM sees should be `got:expected-item`.

### Screenshots/Code snippets

A/B on `main` @ `f04cce923` (same script, only the source tree differs):

```
# pristine main
TOOL RESULT SEEN BY LLM: Error executing tool: The future belongs to a different loop than the one specified as the loop argument

# with the proposed patch
TOOL RESULT SEEN BY LLM: got:expected-item
```

### Operating System

macOS Sonoma

### Python Version

3.11

### crewAI Version

1.15.33 (source checkout of `main` @ `f04cce923`)

### crewAI Tools Version

1.15.33

### Virtual Environment

Venv

### Evidence

Stack shape on `main`: the sync lane runs the tool call in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread` in the flow runtime / `AgentExecutor`), and the native tool path ends in `Tool.run`, whose async branch calls `asyncio.run(self._arun(**kwargs))`. That fresh loop cannot await objects owned by the kickoff caller's loop, and `asyncio.wait_for`/`Future.__await__` raises `RuntimeError: ... different loop`.

This also silently degrades tools that are correct but not loop-independent: an `httpx.AsyncClient` created before kickoff raises on first use, and the exception is swallowed into the tool result string, so the agent reports a tool error instead of a crash.

### Possible Solution

Capture the kickoff caller's loop at the async entry points (`Crew.kickoff_async`, `AgentExecutor.invoke_async`) in a `ContextVar` — ContextVars propagate through `asyncio.to_thread` and the flow runtime's `copy_context`, so every worker lane can see it. Then, in the native tool execution helper, when a caller loop is present **and** the tool has a real async implementation, run the coroutine on that loop (e.g. `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(tool.arun(**args), caller_loop).result()`, which blocks only the worker thread). Fall back to the exact historical `run()` path for sync tools, sync callers, closed loops, or when already on the target loop.

Sync/`kickoff()` behavior must stay byte-identical; `available_functions` should remain authoritative so cache wrappers and test doubles keep working.

### Additional context

Happy to take this one — I have a patch with regression coverage ready (unit tests for the bridge, sync fallbacks, exactly-once error propagation, and an end-to-end `kickoff_async` test that fails on pristine `main` with the error above and passes with the patch). Will link the PR once this issue exists so the contribution meets the "open issue required" rule.

title: [BUG] create_model_from_schema crashes on draft-07 tuple-form items
body:
## Description

`create_model_from_schema` supports `"type": "array"` with a single `items` schema, but it crashes when `items` is a list of positional schemas (JSON Schema draft-07 tuple validation). The 2020-12 equivalent, `prefixItems`, is ignored entirely and silently degrades to an untyped `list`.

In `_json_schema_to_pydantic_type`, the value of `items` is passed straight into the recursive call, which then reads `json_schema.get("$ref")`. A list has no `.get`, so the whole conversion fails with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`.

This is reachable from MCP tool registration (`MCPToolResolver._json_schema_to_pydantic`), so a server that declares a tuple-typed argument breaks tool discovery for every tool it exposes. It is also reachable from `structured_tool._deserialize_schema` when a stored tool `args_schema` is restored.

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from crewai.utilities.pydantic_schema_utils import create_model_from_schema

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "pair": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "integer"}],
        },
    },
    "required": ["pair"],
}
create_model_from_schema(schema)
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../crewai/utilities/pydantic_schema_utils.py", line 1266, in _json_schema_to_pydantic_type
    item_type = _json_schema_to_pydantic_type(
  File ".../crewai/utilities/pydantic_schema_utils.py", line 1170, in _json_schema_to_pydantic_type
    ref = json_schema.get("$ref")
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
```

Reproduced on crewAI 1.15.33. `pydantic_schema_utils.py` is identical on `main` at 97bbfb6.

## Expected behavior

The call returns a model. Positional element schemas should constrain the element type instead of crashing: with the schema above, `pair=["a", 1]` validates and `pair=[None]` is rejected.

## Screenshots/Code snippets

The same failure through the MCP path:

```python
schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"coords": {"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "number"}]}},
}
# MCPToolResolver._json_schema_to_pydantic("tool", schema) -> AttributeError
```

## Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 (the schema path is platform independent)
- Python: 3.12
- crewAI: 1.15.33

A fix should handle both `items: [...]` (draft-07) and `prefixItems: [...]` (2020-12). Flattening the positional schemas into one element union (`list[Union[...]]`) keeps the existing single-schema behavior unchanged and never rejects an array the schema considers valid, because tuple-form `items` allows extra elements unless `additionalItems`/`items` is `false`.

This issue and the linked pull request were prepared with AI assistance.

title: fix(qdrant): isolate per-search filter conditions
body:
## Related issue
Fixes #8884

## Summary
Searching `red` then `blue` with a configured Qdrant filter appended both conditions to its shared `must` list, so the second search returned nothing and later calls retained old constraints. Deep-copy the configured filter before appending a per-call condition.

## Verification
- [x] A real local `:memory:` Qdrant collection, fixed embeddings, and three records exercise consecutive red, blue, and unfiltered searches. The configured tenant filter continues excluding the other tenant; the original filter remains unchanged.
- [x] Three parameterized cases cover no configured filter, an empty `must`, and an existing tenant condition. Before: two fail, one passes. After: all three pass.
- [x] Ruff, Ruff format, mypy, pre-commit, and `git diff --check` pass.

Tested with Python 3.13.12 and qdrant-client 1.20.0. The optional client was installed only in the validation environment; no dependency files changed. The module skips if qdrant-client is unavailable.

Command: `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false uv run --no-sync pytest lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/test_qdrant_filter_isolation.py -o addopts='' --block-network --tb=short -q`.

## Additional context
No live Qdrant server or embedding API was used. This changes only copy isolation, not filtering semantics.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Single-line copy behavior fix in the vector search tool with no auth or data-model changes; regression covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where **each search reused and mutated** the shared `QdrantConfig.filter`, so `filter_by` / `filter_value` conditions stacked in `must` and later queries could return no results.
> 
> **`QdrantVectorSearchTool._run`** now calls **`model_copy(deep=True)`** instead of a shallow copy before appending per-call field conditions, so the configured filter stays unchanged across calls.
> 
> Adds **`test_qdrant_filter_isolation`**, an in-memory Qdrant test (skipped without `qdrant-client`) that runs red, blue, and unfiltered searches in sequence and asserts results and that the original configured filter is unchanged—covering no filter, empty `must`, and a tenant constraint.
